keyFindings: Cushioning: DNA Tuned midsole is soft (on the firmer side of soft) with a rounded, softer heel landing and added 2 mm forefoot foam; heel-to-forefoot transition feels smooth and impact protection is geared for daily mileage comfort.
Responsiveness: The forefoot is described as more poppy/responsive with a touch of resilience, but overall energy return is moderate and best at easy-to-daily paces rather than fast, snappy efforts.

Stability: This is a true neutral shoe with limited formal stability features; lockdown is strong (secure upper, stiff padded heel counter, no heel slippage), while gentle sole flaring/slightly wide platform provide mild lateral support and flexibility remains mild-to-moderate rather than rigid.
Durability: Outsole durability is expected to be good, with substantial rubber coverage and ridged tread providing solid grip and likely strong underfoot wear resistance over time.

Cushioning: Very plush, soft, and protective ride with a high 38 mm heel / 30 mm forefoot stack; heel cushioning feels especially good and forgiving, while the forefoot is also well-cushioned but can feel overly soft/sloppy.
Responsiveness: Energy return is moderate rather than snappy; reviewers repeatedly note limited forefoot pop and that toe-off feels more lively only when pace increases.

Stability: Rearfoot/midfoot stability is decent for a neutral trainer (wide platform, sturdy heel counter, substantial outsole coverage), but forefoot security/lateral hold is weaker due to a stretchy, roomy upper and soft front platform.
Durability: Outsole rubber coverage is deep and extensive, with expected strong wear resistance; early upper durability is positive, with the knit still looking fresh after ~30 miles.

specsDecision: No automatic score/spec change proposed. Conflicts were recorded for reviewer decision.
